quest.title: Flora Investigation Special Lecture
quest.description: There seems to be an event underway near Speranza...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Primogem x20, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Sugar Sculpture: Linnea x2

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: I can't believe it's not just the Moonglow Fireflies... Even cats can get eaten!

dialogues.speaker: Maisie
dialogues.text: Uhm, Jurva... Make sure you keep a close eye on Pavlov the next time you take him for a walk.

dialogues.speaker: Jurva
dialogues.text: Don't worry so much! Pavlov's a lot bigger than a cat. Besides, they're just plants. What's the worst they could do?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: I remember a certain fresh-faced adventurer saying something similar, right before coming face-to-face with a Hexadecatonic Mandragora...

dialogues.speaker: Jurva
dialogues.text: Uhm...

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: Hexadecatonic Mandragora... Awesome!

dialogues.speaker: Lumi
dialogues.text: Ya-ho!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wha— What're you all hollering about, huh? Paimon heard the commotion from miles away! Is this some sort of class?

dialogues.speaker: Maisie
dialogues.text: Yep, it sure is! Linnea's telling us all about her recent findings.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That sounds fun. Can we sit in?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Of course! Please take a seat.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Since we're on the subject of Hexadecatonic Mandragoras, there's another notable variety of plant that can be found near Voidsea Outlook...

dialogues.speaker: Jurva
dialogues.text: You must mean Winter Icelea!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Spot on! I'm talking about Winter Icelea.

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: Hey, Jurva, that's cheating! Linnea didn't even finish asking!

dialogues.speaker: Jurva
dialogues.text: Ah, sorry... I got carried away and jumped the gun. Don't worry, there'll be plenty more questions to answer, right, Linnea?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Enough for everyone! Get your answers at the ready, and you'll all have the chance to earn yourselves a sugar sculpture!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Ooh, a sweet, sweet, sugary reward! Come on, {NICKNAME}, this is our time to shine!

choices.text: I won't go easy on them just because they're children!

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Right! Back to the topic at hand... There's actually an interesting story about Winter Icelea.

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Legend has it that this plant held a deep connection to the "King of Winter Icelea." Now, the "King of Winter Icelea" had a brother, whose own symbolic plant is something you should all be very familiar with... Can anyone tell me what it is?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, Paimon's definitely familiar with those! But that's probably not the right answer...

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Incorrect! The correct answer is — Midsommar Berries.

response.speaker: Mikko
response.text: Midsommar Berries! All I know is Katya and Aino both make delicious Midsommar Torte...

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Midsommar Berries are the symbol of the "King of Midsommar Oak", brother to the "King of Winter Icelea." Legend has it that these two twins have been fighting since birth...

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: They each take turns killing the other, only to be resurrected once more. Each rules their own season, with this cycle of death and rebirth continuing until the end of time.

response.speaker: Maisie
response.text: That's so sad... Despite being connected by blood...

response.speaker: Mikko
response.text: Katya once told me good relationships have nothing to do with blood. Sometimes, it's precisely those connections that cause conflict to arise.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This story is about the changing of the seasons, right?

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: How very perceptive of you! You're right, of course. That's exactly what the scholars of Snezhnaya think this story represents.

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: What's more, due to Winter Icelea's hardiness and resistance to the cold, it's also considered to be a symbol of the Lightkeepers.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "Though the flower may fail..."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "The leaves will keep their promise." Paimon's heard that saying before!

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: It's a very old saying, and hardly anyone still uses it nowadays. I'm surprised you're even aware of it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, we're seasoned adventurers, which means we're... What was it, again? Oh yeah, "well-traveled and well-read"!

response.speaker: Mikko
response.text: The Lightkeepers... They're the ones who dress in black, right?

response.speaker: Mikko
response.text: Are they also hardy and resistant to the cold? But their clothes look so warm... If they really are so resistant, couldn't they wear a bit less?

response.speaker: Maisie
response.text: You've got it all muddled up. What Linnea means is that, just like Winter Icelea, the Lightkeepers stand tall in the face of hardships as fierce as the icy wind.

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Wonderful! Your interpretation is spot on, but let me ask — how did you arrive at that understanding?

response.speaker: Maisie
response.text: Hehe, Helka sent me a handbook, all the way from Fontaine. She told me about the language of flowers. Now all the flowers of Fontaine have their own secret meanings.

response.speaker: Maisie
response.text: I think if Winter Icelea has a meaning, it must be something like... "unbending," or maybe "the courage to persevere until the end."

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Well, someone's clearly learning to draw inferences. Well done!

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: And Mikko... You may have approached it from a very different angle, but your sense of logic is certainly interesting!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Ooh, ooh, Ms. Linnea... What about Paimon and me?

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Hmm, let's see if you two can answer this next one...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Ask away! No question's too hard for {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Such confidence! In that case, I'll ask you one of my hardest. Why do Nocturnal Blossoms come in both red and blue?

choices.text: Because "Roses are red, violets are blue"...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhm...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright... So what's the answer? Nocturnal Blossoms aren't the only things we've seen in Nod-Krai that are red and blue. Come to think of it, we've seen red and blue stuff all over the place!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you're asking about the one thing that stands out most about Nod-Krai...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It must be the extraordinary power of kuuvahki!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Stop trying to explain everything away with "the power of kuuvahki"! There's no way the answer's gonna be as obvious as that!

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: You're... correct!

response.speaker: Lumi
response.text: Ya-hoho!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hu— What! Seriously!?

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: It's common knowledge for those of us who live in Nod-Krai, but not so much for adventurers visiting from afar. So, in context, I suppose it could be considered a tricky problem?

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: But you weren't fooled by the question at all. It looks like you're on the path to becoming a real stellar adventurer!

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Alright, that's it for today. All the students who answered a question can have a sugar sculpture!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Wait a second, don't tell Paimon that she's the only one who doesn't get any candy! If Paimon had known, she'd have answered more questions... even if she'd have probably gotten them all wrong...

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: #Don't worry, don't worry, you'll get yours too! You and {NICKNAME} are a team, just like Lumi and me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Isn't that wonderful, Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, Ms. Linnea really is the best teacher ever!

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: That's certainly a novel answer! But unfortunately... no, that's incorrect.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good thinking! Mint and Winter Icelea are both green... That means Cabbage must be a close relative, too!

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Incorrect! The correct answer is — Midsommar Berries.

choices.text: I wonder if it's Midsommar Berries.

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Correct! The answer is Midsommar Berries.

choices.text: It'll be like taking candy from kids!

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Don't worry, I'll let you in on a secret — Katya's prepared enough sugar sculptures for everyone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! In that case, we'll have to show them just how smart we are!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: There's another legend that claims the opposing colors of the Nocturnal Blossom represent two sisters from the Frostmoon Scions...

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: Do they kill each other, too? I noticed that lots of stories have siblings who end up killing each other. What's up with that? We're not like that in the Conch Gang.

dialogues.speaker: Maisie
dialogues.text: Hey, let Linnea finish the story, will you? I bet the sisters make up in the end, right?

dialogues.speaker: Maisie
dialogues.text: Otherwise, why would people use the Nocturnal Blossom with its two flowers joined together to represent them? ...I hope they make up in the end.

dialogues.speaker: Jurva
dialogues.text: Linnea's always dashing off to here, there, and everywhere, but she still makes time to share her knowledge with us... I've learned a lot from her, and I'm grateful for that.
